top_module.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
top_module.description: Top-level adaptive aero control controller and MMIO endpoint. It owns the register-mapped control/status plane, request packaging, response validation, timeout/staleness monitoring, safe fallback control, actuator output staging, and interrupt generation. It is the required design top and directly exposes the external surrogate request/response transports and actuator outputs.
top_module.functionality: Implements a compact 64-bit register-mapped control/status interface and bounded 64-bit request/response transport around an external surrogate service. It must create one outbound transaction per launch when enabled, include monotonic sequence numbering, request type tagging, compact operating-point metadata, and DrivAerML reference identifiers in the request payload, and must hold request valid until ready is observed. It must accept responses only when valid, matching the expected sequence/token, within timeout, and within programmed bounds. It must clamp any accepted actuator suggestion to configured min/max limits, optionally apply step limiting, and emit only the final bounded command. It must detect timeout, stale-response, protocol, and range faults, enter deterministic fallback on fault or disable, and provide telemetry, interrupt, and status readback. It must remain agnostic to raw geometry payload size and never emit an unclamped actuator command.
responsibilities: Own the external MMIO register window and implement address decode, status readback, and error reporting.
Package outbound 64-bit surrogate requests containing sequence number, request type, operating-point metadata, and compact model identifiers.
Maintain outstanding-request state, launch gating, request retry hold, and optional limited pipelining.
Validate inbound surrogate responses for validity, sequence freshness, timeout, and command range compliance.
Clamp accepted actuator suggestions to configured min/max limits and optional step bounds.
Generate deterministic safe fallback commands and fault status bits on disable, reset, timeout, or validation failure.
Drive registered actuator outputs with valid and mode encoding for normal, fallback-hold, and fault-safe states.
Assert status_irq according to configuration on response acceptance, timeout, or fault entry.
Expose telemetry fields including state, busy/idle, outstanding count, last accepted sequence, timeout/stale/protocol/clamp/fallback indicators, and response counter.
top_module.reset_behavior: On rst_n deassertion, clear outstanding requests, clear request and response valid outputs, initialize actuator_cmd to the programmed fallback value or a conservative default, assert fallback active, clear fault latches unless sticky-fault retention is enabled, set state to idle, zero counters and sequence tracking deterministically, and deassert status_irq until a configured event occurs.
behavior_rules: surrogate_req_valid must remain asserted until surrogate_req_ready is observed.
The top must never depend on a child-only driver for any required top-level output; every top-level output must have a real RTL driver in this module.
Request launch occurs only when enabled, launch bit is asserted, and no outstanding request violation exists under the configured outstanding limit.

Responses are accepted only if surrogate_rsp_valid is high, the sequence/token matches the active request or pipeline window, the response is fresh relative to timeout/freshness thresholds, and range checks pass.
A valid accepted response may update the actuator command only after clamping and optional step limiting.
Invalid, malformed, stale, out-of-range, or late responses are discarded and must not update the actuator output.
Timeout expiry, stale detection, protocol failure, disabled state, or any validation failure must force safe fallback and set the corresponding fault status.
Actuator outputs must always be registered, bounded, and mode-encoded; unclamped command emission is forbidden.
Unsupported MMIO addresses must assert mmio_error for the access and leave control state unchanged aside from any side-effect-free read behavior.

If sticky-fault mode is disabled, a valid new command may clear transient faults only after explicit fault_clear or defined acceptance rules; if enabled, fault retention persists until cleared by firmware.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_control_regfile
modules.description: Compact 64-bit MMIO register file and decode block for control, status, timeout, limits, fallback, operating-point metadata, request sequencing, and interrupt configuration. It exposes semantic configuration fields to the rest of the design and returns 64-bit read data and error indication for unsupported addresses.
modules.functionality: Provides a compact register map with control-enable, soft reset, launch, timeout, min/max limit, fallback, fault-clear, sticky-fault, pipelining, outstanding limit, and status readback fields. It must decode legal addresses, support readback of configuration and telemetry, and assert mmio_error on unsupported or malformed accesses. It also exports compact operating-point metadata including representative velocity, velocity fraction, reference identifier, geometry identifier, request type tag, sequence seed, and session rollover control. All outputs are semantic control fields used by downstream logic; transport buses remain separate.
responsibilities: Decode MMIO reads and writes into semantic configuration fields.
Provide deterministic reset values and write masking via mmio_wstrb.
Expose status and telemetry readback to firmware.
Support control of launch, enable, fault clear, sticky-fault retention, and session rollover behavior.
Provide compact operating-point fields sufficient for 20 to 55 m/s envelope and the representative 38.89 m/s operating point.
Return mmio_error for unsupported addresses or invalid accesses.
Hold configuration stable until rewritten by firmware.
modules.reset_behavior: On rst_n deassertion, initialize control fields to safe defaults: enable low, launch low, soft-reset low, fault-clear low, sticky-fault disabled by default or retained per configuration policy, outstanding limit set to single outstanding, timeout and freshness thresholds to conservative nonzero values, min/max command bounds to a safe envelope, fallback command to a conservative aero-safe value, and telemetry readback fields to zero or idle-indicative values.
behavior_rules: Semantic outputs must be explicit ports and may not be derived implicitly from raw write data in downstream modules.
A read or write must not alter any field outside its addressed register group.
Sequence seed and session rollover settings are used by request packaging and stale-response detection.
Velocity fields are compact metadata only; no raw geometry payload is accepted here.
The register file may not drive top-level transport or actuator outputs directly; it only supplies semantics and telemetry to controller blocks.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_request_packager
modules.description: Packages outbound 64-bit surrogate requests from semantic configuration, request sequencing, and launch control. It emits a single request transaction per accepted launch, embeds monotonically incrementing sequence number, request type tag, operating-point metadata, and compact DrivAerML identifiers, and holds valid until ready is observed.
modules.functionality: Constructs a bounded 64-bit request word carrying the next sequence number, request type, compact operating point, compact model identifiers, and control metadata. It must hold surrogate_req_valid until surrogate_req_ready is observed and must not issue a new request while an outstanding request is already active unless pipelined mode and outstanding count allow it. The block exports request acceptance and active sequence status to downstream monitor and validator logic.
responsibilities: Form outbound request payloads from semantic configuration fields.
Manage one-at-a-time request issue by default, or limited pipelined issuance when configured.
Hold request valid until ready handshake completes.
Generate the active sequence number for validation and timeout tracking.
Assert request issuance only when enabled and launch is requested.
Provide a clean boundary between register semantics and transport payload encoding.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, clear surrogate_req_valid, zero the outbound request word, clear launch acceptance, and initialize the active sequence state from the configured seed or deterministic reset seed as appropriate. The packager must return to idle issuance state with no outstanding request assumptions.
behavior_rules: surrogate_req_valid must stay asserted once a request is launched until surrogate_req_ready is sampled high.
The request data word must include a monotonically incrementing sequence component and a request type tag.
The packager must not alter request payload fields while valid is held unless a new launch is explicitly accepted after handshake completion.
Sequence rollover behavior must be controlled by the session rollover bit and monitored by downstream stale detection logic.
Request issuance must be inhibited when disabled or when outstanding limit is reached.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_response_validator
modules.description: Validates inbound surrogate responses against the expected sequence, freshness, and range rules, then produces safe bounded actuator suggestions and fault classification for the controller. It also contributes response counters and acceptance strobes.
modules.functionality: Consumes valid response traffic from the external surrogate service and checks that each response is marked valid, matches the active request sequence/token, is not stale, and arrives before timeout expiration or freshness threshold violation. When the response contains an actuator-command suggestion, the block interprets it only as a bounded control suggestion, clamps it to configured min/max bounds, optionally step-limits it relative to the previous accepted command, and emits the safe accepted command. Invalid, malformed, stale, or late responses are rejected and classified into fault outputs without updating the actuator command.
responsibilities: Assert surrogate response readiness when able to accept a response.
Parse response data into sequence/token and actuator suggestion fields.
Validate sequence match, freshness, and timeout status.
Classify protocol, timeout, and stale faults separately.
Clamp accepted actuator suggestions to configured bounds and report clamp activity.
Provide accepted command and response acceptance count to controller and telemetry.
Ensure stale-data conditions are reported when session rollover or request age rules indicate stale data.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, deassert surrogate_rsp_ready and acceptance strobes, clear all fault outputs, clear the accepted command to the fallback or conservative value, and reset the response counter and sequence-match state.
behavior_rules: Only responses that are valid, sequence-matched, fresh, and within timeout may be accepted.
A response suggestion must never be passed through unbounded; clamping is mandatory before downstream use.
Stale session events or sequence-age violations must trigger stale fault classification and prevent command update.
The validator must not create combinational dependency loops with the request packager or controller.
The accepted command output is a semantic control suggestion, not a final top-level actuator output.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_timeout_monitor
modules.description: Monitors request age and outstanding request count to detect timeout and freshness violations, handle single-current-request or limited pipelined tracking, and provide stale-data indicators for the controller and validator.
modules.functionality: Maintains a cycle counter for the active request or each outstanding request in the allowed small pipeline, flags timeout when the configured threshold expires without response, and detects stale-data conditions from request age, freshness threshold, or session rollover. It provides busy/idle and outstanding-count telemetry and a latched timeout fault indication for safe fallback control.
responsibilities: Track request age for the active request or limited outstanding set.
Assert timeout_expired when configured threshold is exceeded.
Assert stale_session_event when freshness or rollover conditions indicate stale data.
Provide busy and outstanding_count status for telemetry and gating.
Latch timeout fault state until cleared per control policy.
Remain synchronous and bounded to small counter logic only.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, clear request_age, outstanding_count, busy, timeout_expired, stale_session_event, and timeout_fault_latched. The monitor shall return to idle with deterministic counter values.
behavior_rules: Timeout and freshness thresholds must be programmable and enforced synchronously.
A session rollover event must be reflected as stale when it invalidates prior request context.
The monitor must not depend on response payload contents to increment age.
Outstanding count must never exceed the configured limit in normal operation.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_fallback_controller
modules.description: Combines enable/reset/fault/timeout signals with validated command suggestions to select a deterministic safe fallback or normal bounded command. It defines fallback active, fault state, clamp activity, and final command selection semantics.
modules.functionality: Selects between validated control suggestions and deterministic fallback command based on enable, reset, timeout, stale, and protocol fault conditions. It asserts fallback_active whenever the system is disabled, in reset, or in fault-safe mode, and maintains a stable safe command until cleared per firmware policy. It also tracks fault classification outputs and clamp activity for telemetry.
responsibilities: Choose safe fallback command whenever the system is disabled, in reset, or any fault is present.
Hold a deterministic fallback command stable until explicit clear or accepted new command policy allows change.
Propagate fault classification bits for timeout, stale, and protocol failure.
Forward only bounded and optionally step-limited command suggestions to the actuator stage.
Respect sticky-fault retention behavior when configured.
Provide a safe command that is conservative for aero control and valid across the supported envelope.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, assert fallback_active, clear fault_active unless sticky-fault retention explicitly preserves a latched condition, and drive safe_cmd to cfg_fallback_cmd or a conservative default. The controller must return to a safe stable state with no transient outputs.
behavior_rules: No unclamped command may pass to the output stage.
Fallback command selection must be deterministic and stable.
Fault_clear may release transient faults only according to sticky-fault policy.
Disable or reset always forces fallback active.
Clamp activity must reflect any min/max or step-limit correction applied to the accepted command.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_actuator_output_stage
modules.description: Registers the final 32-bit actuator output, output-valid flag, and 2-bit mode encoding. It guarantees that only bounded commands are emitted and that mode indicates normal closed-loop update, fallback hold, or fault-safe state.
modules.functionality: Pipelines the final actuator command path and encodes mode to identify normal closed-loop update, fallback hold, or fault-safe state. The output command must always be the registered safe command supplied by the fallback controller and may never be an unclamped value. The stage also emits an update pulse for telemetry and downstream timing analysis.
responsibilities: Register the final command and valid indication.
Encode actuator_mode according to normal, fallback, and fault-safe behavior.
Ensure output is stable across cycles when no new update occurs.
Provide a registered update pulse when a command is accepted or fallback state changes.
Never emit an unclamped or unbounded actuator command.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, drive actuator_cmd to the fallback command default, deassert actuator_valid, place actuator_mode in fallback-hold or fault-safe reset state as defined by control policy, and clear update pulses. The stage must come up stable and bounded.
behavior_rules: actuator_valid may only assert for a registered final command.
actuator_mode must distinguish normal update, fallback hold, and fault-safe states.
No top-level actuator output may bypass this stage.
The stage must not change command magnitude outside the safe command provided by the controller.
Update pulses are for telemetry and must not create combinational feedback.

modules.name: adaptive_aero_telemetry_status
modules.description: Aggregates state machine and health telemetry including busy/idle, outstanding request count, last accepted sequence, fault flags, clamp and fallback indicators, and response counter. It also forms the status IRQ pulse/level behavior based on configuration and events.
modules.functionality: Exposes current controller state and health telemetry to firmware and asserts status_irq according to register configuration on response acceptance, timeout, or fault entry. It can operate as a level or latched indicator depending on the internal policy, but must be synchronous and deterministic.
responsibilities: Provide status IRQ behavior tied to acceptance, timeout, and fault events.
Aggregate telemetry fields for readback by the register file.
Maintain deterministic IRQ clear behavior under cfg_status_clear and reset.
Ensure all telemetry signals are synchronized and stable for MMIO readout.
Expose current state machine state and health indicators without modifying them.
modules.reset_behavior: On reset, deassert status_irq and clear any latched IRQ state unless sticky retention is specifically configured outside the normal path. Telemetry readback must reflect idle and fault-cleared reset conditions.
behavior_rules: IRQ behavior must be synchronized to clk and driven only by this telemetry/status block or top-level integration using its output.
Acceptance, timeout, and fault events may independently trigger IRQ according to configuration bits.
Status clear must release latched interrupt behavior without disturbing unrelated control state.
Telemetry values must track the active controller state without hidden derivation.
